question: Paracetamol at therapeutic doses (500–1000 mg) is as effective as ibuprofen for reducing joint inflammation in a patient with active synovitis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Paracetamol has analgesic and antipyretic properties but lacks clinically meaningful anti-inflammatory activity. Its COX inhibition occurs primarily in the CNS, not at peripheral inflammatory sites. For active joint inflammation, paracetamol reduces pain perception but does NOT reduce swelling or the underlying inflammatory process — an NSAID or corticosteroid is needed.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Paracetamol is an effective analgesic and antipyretic but has negligible anti-inflammatory activity at therapeutic doses. Its mechanism is primarily central (inhibiting COX in the brain and spinal cord), while peripheral prostaglandin synthesis — the driver of tissue inflammation — is minimally affected. For active synovitis, an NSAID or corticosteroid is required.
